summary: Ferdinand von Eckstein worked in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen and at Heidelberg University (~1807–1809) under Friedrich Creuzer, later holding a membership at the Société Asiatique.

Ferdinand von Richthofen, a specialist in history and archaeology, studied at the University of Breslau (~1850–1853) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1856). He held posts at Bonn (~1875–1883), Leipzig (~1883–1886), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1886–1905).

Working in Indology and philosophy, he studied at the University of Pisa under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè and Carlo Formichi, and at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held professorships at Pisa (1904–1909, 1914–1952) and Florence (1919–1952).

Ferenc Ruzsa works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (~1971–1975) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982), where he later served as a kari munkatárs around 1993.

Fernand Brunner was a scholar in philosophy who studied at the University of Lausanne (~1938–1942) and the University of Paris (~1946–1951). He served as a professor at the University of Neuchâtel (1954–1986) and taught at Bern (1956–1985).

Fernand Grenard worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He completed his studies at Sciences Po / École Libre des Sciences Politiques (~1885–1888) and INALCO / École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1886–1889).

Fernand Meyer is a Tibetologist who held posts at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique, the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2004), and the Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research (2016).
Fernando Jose Benetti works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University, completing doctoral research under the supervision of Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Tola studied at the National University of San Marcos. He served as a professor at the University of Buenos Aires (attested 1989) and as director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (attested 2001).
Filip Rucinski specializes in Indology and philosophy. He pursued his education at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 2000 to 2006 and earned an M.A. from the University of Warsaw in 2009.

Fortunatov worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Moscow State University, Tübingen, Berlin, Leipzig, and Paris under scholars including Petrov, Roth, Weber, and Bergaigne. He held appointments at Moscow State University from 1875 and joined the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1898.

Filippo De Filippi worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Over the course of his career, he held academic posts at the University of Genoa and the University of Bologna.

Filippo Marsili specializes in Sinology and history and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and under Corrado Pensa, Arcangela Santoro, and Paolo Daffinà, later holding a post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).

Gerety specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Harvard University (2007–2015) under Michael Witzel, held a postdoc at Yale (2017–2018), was a visiting assistant professor at Brown (2018–2024), and held a post at Oxford.

Hall was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He taught at Government College University, Lahore (1850–1855), King's College London (1862–1869), and served as Librarian to the India Office (1864–1869).

Geisshuesler works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Lausanne, the University of Bern, and the University of Virginia (supervised by David Germano), later holding positions at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019) and Sydney (2023).
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she taught Jacques Giès.

Deleanu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bucharest, Waseda, Peking University, and Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen). He served as professor at Kansai Medical University (1994–2001) and as professor and director at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2009).

Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Turin (~2009–2013). She held a postdoctoral fellowship at IIAS (2013) and became an Associate Professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" around 2016.

Fokke Sierksma worked in religious studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Groningen (1936–1950) and later served at Leiden University as a lecturer from 1953 and as Professor of History of Religion from 1973.
